newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India bounds ahead on credit easing.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India bounds ahead on credit easing.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) bounded ahead in the absence of any direction from Bombay, after Saturday's cut in bank reserve requirements from the central bank.
"People are marking stock higher in anticipation that Bombay will open higher after the holiday, but I do not think there were many client buyers in the market," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI rose 3.98 points, 6.46 percent, to 65.59 points, with the premium over the local market at 17.89 percent.

Reliance Industries global depositary shares (GDS) closed at 10.50/$11.50 after $10.00/$10.75 on Friday, while Larsen & Toubro rose $1.95 to $15.00/$16.00 and BSES $1.33 to , while Indian Hotels put on $2.04 to $17.75/$18.75 and Indian Hotels $2.0 to $22.00/$23.00.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced two percentage point cut in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) of banks to 10 percent, effective in four stages over the next four months.
Its policy is expected to release funds in to the economy and bolster the stock market.
"This easing had been pretty much expected but it will boost the market. Local brokers are looking for a big gain," said a trader.
The Bombay 30-share index closed at 3,130.21 on Friday and Indian markets are closed for a Hindu festival until Wednesday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended little changed, down 0.09 points at 72.93, a premium of 29.26 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 1.44 points to 832.62.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.19 points at 89.14, a premium of 2.46 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index added 9.20 points to 6,441.15.
